title: Byte ring of ninety-six positions written by a stepping marker and replayed forwards
summary: String symbols are placed on a ring of 96 byte positions by a write marker that steps once per symbol, starting from position 0 at the start mark. After the separator a replay marker starts at position 0 and steps forward, one symbol per step. Pairs are placed at the position named by their address. A 20-bit integer keeps the open bracket types. Episodes come in five fixed formats: a string to reproduce after a separator; address-item pairs followed by probes; two-type bracket prefixes whose next closer must be named; two tables g and f followed by probes answered f(g(x)); and chains of assignments ending in a probe variable.
core_idea: Place a string on a ring of 96 byte positions with a stepping write marker and replay it with a forward marker from position 0.

state.name: Rb
state.meaning: Ninety-six positions of 8 bits on a ring.

update.name: pair placement
update.plain: a pair is placed at Rb[id(address)] = u_t (48 + id for the second table)

update.name: open-bracket integer
update.plain: opener of type b: ob = 2 ob + b; closer: ob = floor(ob / 2)

update.name: string placement
update.plain: a string symbol is placed at Rb[mk] = code of s_t, then mk = (mk - 1) mod 96; a start mark sets mk = 0

readout.name: next bracket
readout.plain: the closer to predict has the type in the lowest bit of ob

readout.name: replay
readout.plain: at the separator rp = 0, the position of the first symbol; each output is Rb[rp], then rp = (rp + 1) mod 96

readout.name: pair lookup
readout.plain: a probe a reads its position; chains and f(g(x)) read the named position again, at most 8 times

learning.description: Each symbol's role is the one of highest posterior given m example episodes, starting from a uniform prior with likelihood 1 for consistent answers and a small floor otherwise.
learning.few_shot_argument: One consistent episode fixes each symbol's role, so m = 6 example episodes per task are enough in the small cases.

complexity.constants_notes: One position access and one marker step per symbol; 96 bytes, two markers and the open-bracket integer, independent of n.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Posterior over symbol roles from m example episodes.

prediction.statement: With m = 6 example episodes of a task (copy and recall at size up to 4, nesting at depth 2, two-hop lookup at table size up to 4, chained assignments of length up to 2), the learned roles are exact and the task is solved with accuracy 1.0 on three seeds.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator (L = 8, 32, 64)
capabilities.prediction: By hand: the write marker places the L symbols and the replay marker reads them back from the first; exact at L = 8, 32 and 64 over up to 256 symbols.
Each address id below 96 has its own position; exact at K = 8, 32 and 64.
The open-bracket integer is exact at depths 2, 4, 8 and 16.

capabilities.task: two-hop lookup f(g(x)) with tables of size 4, 16, 32, and chained assignments of length 1, 4, 8
capabilities.prediction: g at positions 48..79 and f at 0..31; two reads; exact at sizes 4, 16 and 32. At most 8 linked reads; exact at chain lengths 1, 4 and 8.
A string longer than 96 symbols overwrites its own beginning on the ring, so exact copy fails at L = 97.
The role posterior learns each small case from m = 6 example episodes on three seeds.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: An L = 64 copy episode is replayed with a wrong symbol.
Placing a pair changes a position other than the one its address names.

toy_example.description: Placing a three-symbol string and recording the write marker.
toy_example.python:
import json
Rb = [0] * 96
mk = 0
marks = []
for s in [90, 1, 45]:
    Rb[mk] = s
    mk = (mk - 1) % 96
    marks.append(mk)
print(json.dumps({"marks": marks, "position_0": Rb[0]}))
